newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian PM to be replaced - government sources.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian PM to be replaced - government sources.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti will offer his resignation to King Hussein on Wednesday, government sources said.
The sources told Reuters that Kabariti would be replaced by former prime minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, who signed a peace treaty with Israel in October 1994.
Majali was expected to announce a new cabinet in the next day or two, the sources said.

A cabinet reshuffle had been widely expected in recent weeks ahead of Jordan's scheduled November elections. Two-thirds of the current cabinet are members of parliament, who would have to resign their ministerial posts to run again for parliament.
Kabariti had been seen to have the king's support to stay at the head of the new government.

But Jordanian newspapers pointedly remarked this week at his absence from the king's side during a visit to the site where a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls and on the king's trip on Sunday to Jerusalem to pay condolences to families of the victims.
